In this universe, each celestial creature holds the mastery of an element: water, air, earth, or fire. Study these creatures before the sun rises and learn all their secrets because the player with the greatest mastery of the elements at the end of the game wins! On your turn, collect cards representing the same elements by drawing three cards from the pile (and placing the remaining ones into the market) or by picking them from the market. If you can, discard a collection corresponding to a favor token (flush or same value) and take the token. Take a Mastery Tile (optional) 5.2.1 2.1 Reinforce a tile 5.2.2 2.2 Lock a tile 6 End of game 7 Scoring Objective In Mythicals the board game, 2 players have to collect cards of 4 different colors (4 elements). Those cards will be traded for mastery tiles which give victory points. Components 1 board 20 Mastery tiles 16 bonus markers 48 Creature cards 1 Day Card Setup All the mastery tiles are placed (open side) on the board according to their color and victory points. All bonus markers are placed on the right side of the board. Each player receives 2 creatures cards, always of 2 different colors. The deck is formed with the Day card in the last 9 cards. Gameplay Overview The game plays over a series of turns until someone draws the Day card. All players will play one after the other. Player Turn On your turn, you MUST collect cards and then you MAY take a Mastery tile. 1. Collect Cards (required) You must choose between drawing 3 cards from the deck and collect 1 to 3 drawn cards of the same color OR collect all the cards from any reserve (separated by color). If you collect a card you already have, it goes to your opponent. Cards are placed face up as stacks of different colors. NB : there is a BGA user preference to reverse order the cards in the stack. 2. Take a Mastery Tile (optional) You may take up to 1 mastery tile per turn, each tile has its own requirements based on its position on the board (see BGA tooltips). You always need to discard cards from your collection to take a tile (+ take bonus markers on the tile if any). After taking a tile, you may reinforce or lock another one on the board. NB : Players' tiles are stacked in a way you only see the top one. 2.1 Reinforce a tile Choose an open side (ie. not locked) tile and choose to place 1 or 2 bonus markers on it. 2.2 Lock a tile Choose an open side (ie. not locked) tile with no bonus marker and click the button "LOCK" (or the lock icon), the tile is flipped to its locked side which cannot receive any bonus markers. End of game When the Day card is drawn from the deck, this is the last turn and the current player finishes the turn normally except locking/reinforceing is disabled (because it is useless). Scoring Each bonus marker count as 1 point Each taken Mastery tile gives an amount written on it No tie breaker. [Rating: 1/10] It doesn't overstay its welcome! Because it wasn't welcome in the first place.  There’s some potential, at least a little interaction, but just goes nowhere because everything is too calculable. And it’s too short and minimalist for the unknowns to be suspenseful either, so just be efficient!

[Rating: 2/10] I get the idea but the artwork doesn't appeal to me and the scoring feels weird with the locking thing. There are many more set collection kind of games that I would prefer to play.

[Rating: 3/10] Tried one game.  Basic choices, not a lot to enjoy.  Aesthetically beautiful, but very poor gamewise

[Rating: 3/10] Honestly, don't bother. The only reason I have even given this game a 3* is due to its interesting art style and slick design when it comes to storage and tabletop layout.   As a local game store employee I am blessed with the opportunity of play testing games most days. This on the other hand was a personal purchase.   After playing it with my partner I felt well and truly underwhelmed. This game, at its core, struggles to make players feel both rewarded or engaged.   I feel this game may suit a much younger audience (children aged around 6-10) despite the game being rated 8+.   Any avid boar

[Rating: 4/10] Fun little filler. Like all of them very reliant on card draw . Kind of column trick taking that is turn based eg Rummy. Quick and pretty smooth.  After playing this over 20 times the first player gets a distinct advantage in that they may get an additional turn. This should be balanced by a 1 point token given to the second player. But I am still not sure that would balance out this game. Maybe one card from the deck be played faceup in the area at the beginning of the game too? [Rating: 4.5/10] Played on BGA.  Super basic, not very interesting. Just collecting cards and turning in sets of different ones of the same number or consecutive numbers of the same suit for points. Slight tweak where you're allowed to increase the points of something else when you you turn in another set, but other than that..... that's it.  Nothing is broken about the game, but this is about as bland of a set collection game as there is. I think I'd rather play Gin Rummy over this. At least that has more to keep track of.
